title: 8-Quinolinolate complexes of yttrium and ytterbium: molecular arrangement and fragmentation under laser impact

synthesis.procedure: All manipulations were carried out under vacuum using standard Schlenk techniques. A solution of Cp3Y (125 mg, 0.44 mmol) in warm DME (5 ml) was added to a solution of 8-hydroxyquinoline (192 mg, 1.32 mmol) in warm DME (10 ml). The mixture was stirred for 15 min at 60 °C and then cooled slowly to room temperature to give yellow crystals of Y3Q9 containing a solvate DME molecule.
synthesis.temperature: 60 °C, then cooled slowly to room temperature
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling of the DME reaction mixture afforded yellow crystals of the DME solvate.

properties.summary: This paper primarily characterizes 1 structurally. Ligand-centered electroluminescence of 1 in a bilayer OLED is reported as a broad band peaking at 530 nm (previously measured, efficiency comparable to AlQ3). No magnetic data are given.

measurements.name: electroluminescence peak (ligand-centered)
measurements.conditions: bilayer OLED; previously reported for 1; ligand-centered emission

synthesis.procedure: Complex 2 was obtained analogously to 1 under vacuum Schlenk conditions from Yb[N(SiMe3)2]3 (103 mg, 0.16 mmol) and 8-hydroxyquinoline (69 mg, 0.48 mmol) in DME (warmed, stirred 15 min at 60 °C, then cooled slowly to room temperature), affording yellow crystals of the DME solvate.
synthesis.temperature: 60 °C, then cooled slowly to room temperature (same conditions as 1)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk techniques under vacuum; analogous procedure to 1
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Isolated as yellow crystals of the DME solvate upon cooling.

properties.summary: In a three-layer OLED (ITO/TPD/2/BATH/Yb), complex 2 shows ligand-centered EL at 530 nm and Yb3+ metal-centered NIR emission at 979 nm (2F5/2 → 2F7/2). Maximum NIR irradiance is 50 μW cm−2, much lower than related naphtholate/phenolate Yb emitters and consistent with conventional singlet–triplet–Ln energy transfer rather than Yb3+/Yb2+ redox sensitization. Used as the emissive layer.
